key_insight: Kinetic non-equilibrium can strongly alter hypersonic temperature and heat-flux disturbances even when Navier–Stokes predictions of wall pressure remain close.
engineering_relevance: Resolving rarefaction near shocks and walls can improve high-altitude hypersonic receptivity analysis, especially for thermal-response assessment.
method: Linearize the discrete unified gas-kinetic scheme using complex, time-harmonic perturbations.
Solve the resulting steady disturbance system by pseudo-time marching with LU-SGS acceleration.
Capture shock structure, wall slip, temperature jumps, and non-Fourier heat flux without hybrid coupling.
evidence_signal: Three benchmarks verify the framework; argon blunt-wedge cases at equivalent altitudes of 40 and 50 km show increasing kinetic effects, with pronounced thermal-disturbance differences at 50 km.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported benchmarks and argon wedge cases; broader gas models and geometries require further validation.
paper_title: Kinetic Non-Equilibrium Receptivity Analysis of Hypersonic Flows via a Complex Linearized Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme
